headline: Funding flows. Contracts expand. Diplomacy signs.
deck: This week, space firms are diversifying their portfolios while governments are signing treaties like it's 1999.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M, eyes co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. This capital will bolster its capabilities in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas that are becoming increasingly critical for national defense. With the DoD's growing interest, this funding could be a game-changer for their operational reach.
stories.soWhat: When the government starts pulling through, it's like finding a $20 bill in your winter coat—unexpected but very welcome.

stories.head: Rocket Lab scores big with launch contract
stories.body: Rocket Lab announced its largest launch contract to date, though the exact dollar amount remains undisclosed. This comes as the company also looks to acquire a space robotics firm, indicating a strategy to broaden its service offerings beyond just launches. The dual focus on launches and robotics suggests Rocket Lab is positioning itself for a more integrated role in space operations.
stories.soWhat: If Rocket Lab can pull off both, they'll be the Swiss Army knife of small satellite launches, which is a pretty nifty tool to have.

stories.head: Paraguay joins Artemis Accords, diplomacy heats up
stories.body: Paraguay recently signed the Artemis Accords, becoming the sixth country to do so. This move illustrates a growing trend where nations are aligning themselves with U.S. space policy, which could influence future international collaborations and competition. With space treaties becoming the new diplomatic currency, expect more countries to follow suit.
stories.soWhat: When signing treaties becomes the new cool, you know the space race is less about rockets and more about alliances.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Rocket Lab's acquisition
watchlist.body: The outcome of Rocket Lab's potential acquisition could redefine its market position and service capabilities.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser moves forward
watchlist.body: With the critical design review passed, all eyes will be on whether Sierra Space can deliver on its promises.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension implications
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension on the TITAN program could set the stage for future contracts and influence investor sentiment.

watchlist.title: Watch for more countries signing treaties
watchlist.body: As more nations join the Artemis Accords, we could see shifts in international space collaboration and competition.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
